cues.en: Pretty much everyone knows that public transit is more efficient than private cars and moving large numbers of people, but we don't talk enough about just how big the difference is. This is the Don Valley Parkway, a six lane highway in Toronto. If you sit in one place at rush hour and watch the DVP, you could see six to maybe 8,000 people in those cars pass by in the busier direction over the course of an hour. If you do the same thing on the nearby Yonge subway, you could see 30,000 people per direction per hour with ongoing signal upgrades pushing that up to 40,000 people in the future. That's an enormous advantage for the subway even before you consider that it only takes up two lanes, mostly underground.
cues.zh: 几乎所有人都知道公共交通比私家车更高效，能运送大量人群，但我们对这种差距到底有多大讨论得还不够。这是当河谷大道，多伦多的一条六车道高速公路。如果你在高峰时段坐在一个地方观察DVP，一小时内较繁忙方向上你能看到六千到八千人乘车经过。如果你在附近的央街地铁做同样的事，每小时每个方向能看到三万人，随着信号系统持续升级，未来这一数字将提升到四万人。这对于地铁来说是巨大的优势，甚至还没算上它只占用两条车道、且大部分在地下。

cues.en: Subways don't carry freight, but when it comes to carrying lots of people, mass transit wins hands down, and it's not even close. We're gonna come back to this capacity difference later in the video.
cues.zh: 地铁不运货，但说到运送大量人群，公共交通完胜，而且差距悬殊。我们稍后会在视频中回到这个运力差异的话题。

cues.en: If you follow debates about building or expanding roads and highways, you've probably heard someone bring up the concept of induced demand, often linking explainer videos from places like Vox, where they use lots of colorful balls to explain, to argue against building the new road or highway. Induced demand, more accurately called induced traffic, is the idea that building new road space doesn't solve congestion, at least in the long term, because it encourages more driving to happen. When you build new lanes or roads, people who previously avoided driving at rush hour start becoming less careful about when and how much they drive. On top of that, other people and businesses see the new road capacity and move to the area to use it. As a result, congestion eventually ends up about as bad as before, and this is used as an argument against building the new road capacity.
cues.zh: 如果你关注过关于修建或扩建道路和高速公路的辩论，你可能听人提到过诱导需求这个概念，常常还会链接Vox等媒体的解释视频——他们用很多彩色小球来解释，以此反对修建新道路或高速公路。诱导需求，更准确的说法是诱导交通，指的是修建新的道路空间并不能解决拥堵，至少从长远来看如此，因为它会鼓励更多驾驶行为发生。当你修建新车道或新道路时，以前在高峰时段避免开车的人开始不那么在意何时开车、开多少车。除此之外，其他人和企业看到新的道路容量，就搬到该地区来使用它。结果，拥堵最终会变得和之前差不多严重，而这被用来作为反对修建新道路容量的论据。

cues.en: Induced traffic is a very real phenomenon.
cues.zh: 诱发交通是一个非常真实的现象。

cues.en: It's not infinite. You can build a big highway in the middle of nowhere, and it's not gonna become congested in the near future. But there's a bunch of research finding that 50 to 100% of new road capacity in urban areas gets filled up after a few years. However, the induced traffic argument against new car infrastructure has always seemed maybe not wrong, but certainly incomplete.
cues.zh: 它不是无限的。你可以在荒郊野外建一条大高速公路，短期内它不会拥堵。但大量研究发现，城市地区新增道路容量的 50% 到 100% 会在几年后被填满。不过，反对新建小汽车基础设施的诱发交通论点，一直以来可能不算错，但肯定不完整。

cues.en: Because why does it only mention cars? What happens when we build another subway line, for example? Won't that just become packed in a couple of years too? Isn't that a problem? In this video, we're going to explain why induced traffic for walking, biking, and public transit is different than for cars, and why increased demand or usage for a mode doesn't have to mean slower travel for everyone. Let's get back to transit in Toronto. In response to overcrowding on the Yonge Subway, including at the major transfer station with the Bloor Dam fourth line, transit authorities are planning to build a new automated subway called the Ontario line to add capacity to the city's East End. When you think about it, the exact same points about induced traffic and highways could apply here, except that we probably call it induced ridership.
cues.zh: 因为为什么只提小汽车？比如，我们再建一条地铁线会怎样？它不也会在几年后变得拥挤吗？这难道不是问题吗？在本视频中，我们将解释为什么步行、骑行和公共交通的诱发交通与汽车不同，以及为什么某种交通方式的需求或使用量增加，并不一定意味着所有人出行都变慢。让我们回到多伦多的公共交通。为应对 Yonge 地铁的过度拥挤，包括与 Bloor-Danforth 线的主要换乘站，交通部门计划新建一条名为 Ontario Line 的自动化地铁，为城市 East End 增加运力。仔细想想，关于诱发交通和高速公路的完全相同观点也可以套用在这里，只不过我们大概会把它叫作诱发客流。

cues.en: In other words, this new subway line will cause more people to take more trips, both people who currently live there and new people moving to East End Toronto because of the new subway. Ridership will continue to grow, and eventually, at some point in the future, the Ontario line will probably end up congested.
cues.zh: 换句话说，这条新地铁线会让更多人出行更多次，既包括目前住在那里的人，也包括因为新地铁而搬到多伦多 East End 的新居民。客流量会继续增长，最终在未来某个时候，Ontario Line 可能也会变得拥堵。

cues.en: But if you told a transit planner that they shouldn't build the Ontario line because it will just induce more ridership and eventually become congested, they would probably look at you funny. Induced ridership is one of the goals of the Ontario line, which is meant to encourage growth in new transit oriented communities.
cues.zh: 但如果你告诉交通规划师，他们不该建 Ontario line，因为它只会诱发更多客流，最终变得拥挤，他们大概会觉得你很奇怪。诱发客流正是 Ontario line 的目标之一，这条线本意是促进新的公共交通导向型社区发展。

cues.en: We want people to use the Ontario line, whether replacing car trips or taking trips they wouldn't otherwise have been able to do. We prefer that it's not so much new ridership that the new line becomes overcrowded. That's bad for safety, efficiency, and user experience. But if and when that happens, it wouldn't mean the Ontario line was useless and shouldn't have been built in the first place. It would mean the Ontario line was really useful, we should probably build another subway line. If that's not possible, it's still better to have an overcrowded Ontario line than no Ontario line at all. The young subway is overcrowded now, and no one thinks that means it shouldn't have been built.
cues.zh: 我们希望人们使用 Ontario line，无论是替代开车出行，还是完成他们原本没法进行的出行。我们希望新增客流不要多到让新线路变得过度拥挤。那对安全、效率和用户体验都不好。但即便真的发生，也不代表 Ontario line 没用、当初就不该建。那反而说明 Ontario line 真的很有用，我们大概该再建一条地铁线。如果做不到，拥挤的 Ontario line 也总比没有 Ontario line 好。Yonge subway 现在已经很拥挤，也没人觉得这说明它当初不该建。

cues.en: If the basic principle of induced demand is the same, why does car infrastructure inducing more car traffic seem so threatening while public transit infrastructure inducing more transit ridership feels benign or even good? One big reason is what we mentioned at the beginning of this video. The simple fact that public transit can carry a lot more people. So reaching capacity is less of an immediate concern. Imagine we're choosing between two transportation projects in Toronto's East End. The Ontario line with its planned top capacity of 34,000 passengers per hour per direction,
cues.zh: 如果诱发需求的基本原理相同，为什么汽车基础设施诱发更多车流看起来如此可怕，而公共交通基础设施诱发更多客流却显得无害甚至很好？一个重要原因就是我们在这个视频开头提到的。一个简单事实：公共交通能运送多得多的人。所以达到运力上限没那么迫在眉睫。想象一下，我们要在多伦多东区的两个交通项目之间做选择。一个是 Ontario line，规划最高运力为每方向每小时 34,000 名乘客，

cues.en: or a six lane highway resembling the Don Valley Parkway with a six to 8,000 people per hour per direction.
cues.zh: 另一个是类似 Don Valley Parkway 的六车道高速，每方向每小时能运 6,000 到 8,000 人。

cues.en: Both projects will induce more people to take more trips, both have the potential to hit capacity and become overcrowded,
cues.zh: 这两个项目都会让更多人出行，也都有可能达到运力上限，变得拥挤，

cues.en: but one will reach capacity much faster than the other. It's more than that though. It's not just that transit can handle high volumes, it's that transit usually gets better with more ridership. Most of the ways that a transit agency adds capacity to a route makes service better for each individual rider, whether that's higher frequency, using trains over buses, giving signal priority on roads, or making the line tunneled or elevated. Transit riders don't want crowding, but they do have reason to want their routes to be well used. Driving works differently. You want enough other drivers to justify your road or highway existing.
cues.zh: 但其中一个会比另一个更快达到上限。不过，差别还不止于此。公共交通不只是能运送大量乘客，通常乘客越多，服务反而越好。公共交通机构为线路增加运力的许多方式，也会改善每位乘客的体验，比如提高班次频率、用火车替代公交车、为道路上的车辆提供信号优先通行，或将线路改为地下或高架。乘客不希望太拥挤，但也有理由希望自己的线路得到充分利用。开车则不一样。你希望有足够多的其他司机，来证明修建这条道路或高速公路是值得的。

cues.en: But aside from that, traffic is really only a threat that can slow you down or aggravate you. No one wishes for more drivers on their road to get more lanes, but you might wish for more ridership in your transit route so that you can get better frequency. If transit service gets better with more ridership, but the driving experience gets worse with more traffic, it makes sense that induced car traffic feels more threatening than induced transit ridership.
cues.zh: 除此之外，交通流量带来的影响基本只有一种：拖慢你的速度，或让你心烦。没人会希望路上多些司机，好让道路多修几条车道；但你或许会希望公共交通线路有更多乘客，这样班次就能更密。既然公共交通服务会随着乘客增加而改善，而开车体验却会随着交通拥堵加剧而变差，那么诱发的汽车交通比诱发的公共交通客流更让人担忧，也就说得通了。

cues.en: There is one more important difference between transit and driving when it comes to induced demand, which is pricing.
cues.zh: 诱发需求方面，公共交通和开车还有一个重要区别，那就是定价。

cues.en: One simple way to reduce congestion is to charge more money, discouraging people from making less important trips. For transit, this is straightforward. You increase the price of a fare or a pass, ideally offering a low income subsidy if necessary.
cues.zh: 减少拥堵的一个简单办法是提高收费，劝退人们进行不那么重要的出行。对公共交通来说，这很直接。你可以提高单程票价或通票价格，必要时最好提供低收入补贴。

cues.en: The driving equivalent to this would be a road toll or congestion charge, but at least in Canada we're not set up for that. Toll roads are rare and very unpopular.
cues.zh: 开车出行的对应做法是道路收费或拥堵费，但至少在加拿大，我们还没有这样的制度安排。收费道路很少，而且非常不受欢迎。

cues.en: Increasing the gas tax might kind of work as a substitute. People can partially get around that by buying a more fuel efficient car or stocking up on gas in a different jurisdiction.
cues.zh: 提高汽油税或许能起到某种替代作用。人们可以通过购买更省油的车，或到另一个辖区囤汽油，部分绕开这项收费。

cues.en: Thus, another reason that induced demand is less of a problem for public transit is that it has a simple form of congestion pricing built in. We've focused on transit so far, but we fully expect induced demand to apply to walking or cycling infrastructure too. Imagine that your city has a mixed use pathway that's overcrowded, and the local cycling advocacy group wants to double the width of the path so that pedestrians and cyclists have their own dedicated space. This probably will induce more people to walk and cycle. And like with transit, that doesn't sound so bad, whether people are replacing car trips or they're just being more mobile in general. Partly, this is because more physical activity is a win for public health, and partly, is because trips taken by walking and cycling lack the negative externalities of cars. A bunch of people walking and cycling through your neighborhood just doesn't have the same noise, safety, and pollution side effects as the same number of people driving through your neighborhood. Infrastructure for walking and cycling is also relatively cheap and space efficient.
cues.zh: 因此，诱导需求对公共交通来说问题较小的另一个原因，是它内置了一种简单的拥堵定价。到目前为止我们关注的是公共交通，但我们完全预计诱导需求也适用于步行和自行车基础设施。想象一下，你的城市有一条多用途步道过于拥挤，当地自行车倡导团体想把这条件路拓宽一倍，让行人和骑行者各有专用空间。这很可能会诱导更多人步行和骑行。和公共交通一样，这听起来并不坏，无论人们是在替代汽车出行，还是只是总体上出行更多。部分原因是更多身体活动对公共卫生是好事，部分原因是步行和骑行出行没有汽车那样的负外部性。一群人步行和骑行穿过你的社区，和同样数量的人开车穿过你的社区相比，并不会带来同样的噪音、安全和污染副作用。步行和骑行基础设施也相对便宜且节省空间。

cues.en: No neighborhoods are being demolished to build bike lanes, but lots of neighborhoods were erased from existence to build highways in mid century North America.
cues.zh: 没有社区正在因为建自行车道而被拆除，但20世纪中叶的北美，大量社区却因为修高速公路而从地图上消失。

cues.en: Based on these examples, the concept of induced demand on its own is not actually a slam dunk argument against expanding roads or building new highways.
cues.zh: 基于这些例子，诱导需求这个概念本身其实并不是反对扩建道路或新建高速公路的决定性论据。

cues.en: The problem with new car infrastructure isn't only that it'll induce more trips, because the same can be said for a new subway, bike route, or walking path, assuming they're built to conveniently connect people to places they need to go. Instead, the problem with new car infrastructure is related to the specific downsides of cars, from the negative externalities related to noise, safety, pollution, to the basic geometric fact that they're an inefficient way to move a lot of people in a city, which makes them especially prone to congestion,
cues.zh: 新建汽车基础设施的问题不只在于它会诱导更多出行，因为新建地铁、自行车道或步行道也一样——前提是它们能方便地把人连接到需要去的地方。相反，新建汽车基础设施的问题与汽车特有的缺点有关，从噪音、安全、污染相关的负外部性，到一个基本的几何事实：在城市里运送大量人口时汽车效率低下，这让它们特别容易拥堵，

cues.en: even when we dedicate a lot of space to them. Rather than thinking about induced demand as a special property of cars, we should think of induced demand as a basic fact that transportation demand and usage patterns aren't fixed. People make short term choices about how to get around and long term choices about where to live based on the infrastructure available to them. If you build wider roads, people will drive more, and they'll plan their lives around driving. If you build fast and convenient transit lines, people will take transit more and plan their lives around transit. If you build a safe and comfortable bike network that connects people to places they need to go, people will bike more and so on. The question isn't really which types of transportation infrastructure induce demand, because they all do. The question is which type of demand do you want to induce?
cues.zh: 即使我们给它们分配了大量空间。与其把诱导需求看作汽车的特殊属性，不如把它看作一个基本事实：交通需求和使用模式并非固定不变。人们会根据可用基础设施，做出短期出行选择和长期居住地选择。如果你建更宽的道路，人们会开更多车，并围绕开车安排生活。如果你建快速便捷的公交线路，人们会更多乘坐公交，并围绕公交安排生活。如果你建一个安全舒适、连接人们目的地的骑行网络，人们会更多骑车，等等。问题其实不是哪种交通基础设施会诱导需求，因为它们都会。问题是，你想诱导哪种需求？

cues.en: Don't forget to induce bicycle infrastructure demand and subscribe.
cues.zh: 别忘了激发自行车基础设施需求，并订阅。
